**Literature sweep: choosing cluster resolution, judging cluster validity and evaluation pitfalls in single-cell data (2017 to Sept 2026, weighted to 2023 to 2026)**

**Three findings that matter most for the project**
1. Several published, peer-reviewed methods now pick the number of clusters with a statistical test. None of them has been applied to mutual-information (MI) based clustering such as scMINER's MICA.
2. The LLM and knowledge-guided ways of choosing resolution are all recent (late 2025 to 2026), mostly preprints, and none controls for double dipping. The marker genes an LLM reads are computed from the same cells that defined the clusters.
3. No independent benchmark I found includes MICA or scMINER. scMINER's own evaluation has known weak points (details in section 6).

---

### 1. Choosing resolution with a statistical test
- **CHOIR** (Sant, Mucke, Corces; *Nature Genetics* 2025, 57:1309–1319; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-025-02148-8).
  - It first builds a deliberately over-split tree, raising resolution until silhouette is maximized.
  - It then works back up the tree. For each pair of sibling clusters, it trains balanced random forests to tell them apart and compares their accuracy with a permutation null (100 permutations by default). Pairs that cannot be told apart are merged.
  - It was benchmarked on 230 simulated and 5 real datasets, the largest a 3.29M-nucleus human brain atlas, which shows it scales to our Dataset 2 size.
  - Full-text extraction lists competitors including Seurat/Scanpy Louvain and Leiden, SCCAF, sc-SHC, Cytocipher, GiniClust3, CIDR, SAFE-clustering, scCAN, SHARP and Spectrum. The exact list of 15 is UNVERIFIED.
  - Reported results: Seurat over-split homogeneous snATAC populations and under-split a pool of 190 cell lines. sc-SHC avoided over-splitting but tended to under-split.
  - Stated limitations: it costs more than a single Louvain run, and it assumes batch is not confounded with biology.
- **sc-SHC** (Grabski, Street, Irizarry; *Nature Methods* 2023, 20:1196–1202; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-023-01933-9).
  - It extends Significance of Hierarchical Clustering (SHC) to counts, testing each split against a fitted single-population null with family-wise error control.
  - `testClusters()` can audit any existing labeling, including MICA's.
  - Defaults per the README: alpha 0.05 (0.25 suggested for discovery), 2,500 features, 30 PCs (https://github.com/igrabski/sc-SHC).
- **recall** (DenAdel et al.; *American Journal of Human Genetics* 2025; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0002929725000618; code at https://github.com/lcrawlab/recall).
  - It adds knockoff-style artificial null genes, clusters, and requires every cluster pair to show significant differential expression after calibration. If a pair fails, it re-clusters at lower resolution.
  - Discrepancy: the docs give the title "A knockoff calibration method to avoid over-clustering…" and DOI 10.1016/j.ajhg.2025.02.008. The journal title is "Artificial variables help to avoid over-clustering…" and Nature Index shows 10.1016/j.ajhg.2025.02.014. Exact DOI UNVERIFIED.
- **Cytocipher** (*Bioinformatics* 2023, 39(7):btad435; https://academic.oup.com/bioinformatics/article/39/7/btad435/7224247). Starts over-clustered and merges clusters whose marker-set enrichment scores do not differ significantly.
- **SCCAF** (Miao et al.; *Nature Methods* 2020, 17:621–628; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-020-0825-9). Merges clusters based on the confusion matrix of a classifier trained on cluster labels. CHOIR is a statistically calibrated descendant of this idea.

### 2. Stability, consensus and multi-resolution methods
- **SC3** (Kiselev et al.; *Nature Methods* 2017; https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.4236). Consensus k-means, with k estimated from eigenvalues that exceed the Tracy–Widom bound. **SC3s** extends it to millions of cells (*BMC Bioinformatics* 2022; https://doi.org/10.1186/s12859-022-05085-z).
- **chooseR** (Patterson-Cross, Levine, Menon; *BMC Bioinformatics* 2021, 22:39; https://doi.org/10.1186/s12859-021-03957-4). Subsamples 80% of cells, re-clusters, picks the resolution with near-maximal median co-clustering silhouette, and reports per-cluster robustness.
- **MultiK** (Liu, Thennavan, Garay, Marron, Perou; *Genome Biology* 2021; https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-021-02445-5). Subsampling consensus across resolutions, returning several candidate K values.
- **scCCESS** (*BMC Bioinformatics* 2019; https://doi.org/10.1186/s12859-019-3179-5; https://github.com/PYangLab/scCCESS). Ensembles of autoencoders on random projections. K is the most stable choice across the ensemble.
- **IKAP** (Chen et al.; *GigaScience* 2019, 8(10):giz121; https://academic.oup.com/gigascience/article/8/10/giz121/5579995). Tunes PCs and resolution using gap statistics plus how well differentially expressed markers classify the clusters.
- **clustree** (Zappia and Oshlack; *GigaScience* 2018, 7(7):giy083; https://github.com/lazappi/clustree). A visualization of how clusters split across resolutions, not a selection rule.
- **MRtree** (Peng, …, Roeder; *Nucleic Acids Research* 2021, 49(16):e91; https://academic.oup.com/nar/article/49/16/e91/6300355). Reconciles clusterings at many resolutions into one hierarchy and cuts the tree where stability drops sharply.
- **scclusteval** (Tang et al.; *Bioinformatics* 2021, 37(15):2212; https://academic.oup.com/bioinformatics/article/37/15/2212/5962080). Per-cluster Jaccard stability under subsampling.
- **scICE** (Kim et al.; *Nature Communications* 2025; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-60702-8).
  - Uses an "inconsistency coefficient" computed across Leiden runs with different random seeds, so no consensus matrix is needed. A result counts as consistent when median IC < 1.005.
  - Claims up to 30x speedup over multiK and chooseR, tested on 48 datasets.
  - A press release (https://phys.org/news/2025-07-scientists-tackle-cell-reliability-crisis.html) says about two-thirds of existing analyses were unstable. That figure is the press release's claim, not verified in the paper.
- **Stability is not validity.** A stable split can still be driven by noise, batch or cell-cycle signal. CHOIR, sc-SHC and recall exist because stability alone lets in false splits.

### 3. Double dipping and inference after clustering
- **Count splitting** (Neufeld, Gao, Popp, Battle, Witten; *Biostatistics* 2024, 25(1):270–287; https://academic.oup.com/biostatistics/article-abstract/25/1/270/6893953).
  - Binomial thinning splits each count into independent training and test matrices (Poisson assumption, epsilon = 0.5 recommended).
  - You cluster on the training matrix and test on the test matrix.
- **Negative binomial count splitting** (Neufeld et al.; arXiv 2023; https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.12985). Needed because Poisson splitting breaks down under overdispersion. Journal status UNVERIFIED.
- **Data thinning** (Neufeld, Dharamshi, Gao, Witten; *JMLR* 2024, 25(57); https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.07276). Generalizes the idea to any convolution-closed distribution, and the `datathin` package includes a tutorial on choosing K.
- **Selective inference, exact p-values**
  - Hierarchical clustering: Gao, Bien, Witten, *JASA* 2024, 119(545):332–342 (https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.2022.2116331).
  - k-means: Chen and Witten, *JMLR* 2023, 24(152) (https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v24/22-0371.html).
  - Single-feature tests (CADET): Chen and Gao, *Biostatistics* 2025, 26(1):kxae046 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.16375).
  - False discovery rate control via data splitting for testing after clustering: arXiv 2024 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06451).
- **ClusterDE** (bioRxiv 2023, https://doi.org/10.1101/2023.07.21.550107; software paper in *Journal of Computational Biology* 2026, https://doi.org/10.1177/15578666251383562). A synthetic one-cluster null serves as a negative control for post-clustering differential expression. A search snippet says the full method appeared at RECOMB 2025 (UNVERIFIED).
- **Relevance to scMINER.** Its differential driver-activity tests between MICA clusters use the same cells that defined the clusters, which is exactly the double-dipping pattern above. This is my inference; the paper does not discuss it.

### 4. Silhouette and internal metrics
- **Rautenstrauch and Ohler**, "Shortcomings of silhouette in single-cell integration benchmarking" (*Nature Biotechnology* 2025; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-025-02743-4; preprint https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.01.21.634098v1).
  - Silhouette assumes compact, convex clusters, which label-defined single-cell groups often are not.
  - It cannot reliably assess batch removal or biology conservation. They recommend CiLISI plus ARI-type metrics instead.
- **Yerbury et al.** (*ACM TKDD* 19(8), 2025; https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10351). Based on 2.7M partitions, relative validity indices such as silhouette are unsuitable for choosing between similarity paradigms. That is exactly what "MI distance vs PCA-Euclidean judged by silhouette" does.
- **Tomašev and Radovanović**, "Clustering evaluation in high-dimensional data" (Springer, 2016; https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-319-24211-8_4). Hub points sit near cluster centres and shrink between-cluster distances.
- **Counterpoint:** Powell (arXiv 2022; https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.05214) finds most Euclidean validity indices stay sensitive in high dimensions on synthetic data.
- **Sciaraffa et al.** (*Frontiers in Bioinformatics* 2025, 5:1562410; https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/bioinformatics/articles/10.3389/fbinf.2025.1562410/full). Of 15 internal indices, only Banfield–Raftery and within-cluster dispersion predicted accuracy across datasets. Silhouette did worse.
- **Validity-index benchmark:** Simpson, Campello, Stojanovski (arXiv 2025; https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.05983) compare 26 internal indices on more than 16,000 datasets.

### 5. External metrics, rare cell types and hierarchy
- **ARI vs AMI.** Romano, Vinh, Bailey, Verspoor, *JMLR* 2016, 17 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.01286): prefer ARI when reference clusters are large and balanced, and AMI when the reference is unbalanced with small clusters.
- **Pair-counting decomposition.** Warrens and van der Hoef, *Journal of Classification* 2022, 39:487–509 (https://doi.org/10.1007/s00357-022-09413-z): ARI breaks down into per-cluster agreement dominated by large clusters, so rare types barely move it.
- **Choice of null model** also changes chance-adjusted scores: Gates and Ahn (arXiv 2017; https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.06508).
- **Rare cell types**
  - scCAD (*Nature Communications* 2024; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-51891-9) scores rare-type detection with F1 across 25 datasets. Best F1 was only about 0.42, which shows how hard this is.
  - CHOIR adds an entropy-of-accuracy measure to detect under-clustering.
- **Hierarchy-aware metrics**
  - wRI and wNMI weight disagreements by cell-type tree distance: Wu and Wu, *Genome Biology* 2020, 21:123 (https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-020-02027-x).
  - LCAD (lowest-common-ancestor distance on the Cell Ontology) and scGraph-OntoRWR: Wu et al., *Genome Biology* 2025, 26:334 (https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-025-03781-6).
  - Hop-F1: SOCAM preprint 2026 (https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.01.13.699356v1.full).
  - Cell Ontology reference: Tan et al. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.10037). Search says it was published in *Scientific Data* 2026 (UNVERIFIED).

### 6. Knowledge-guided and LLM-guided resolution selection
- **GPTAnno** (Song, Tang, Liu, Wang, Qian, Zou, Hou; bioRxiv Dec 2025; https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.11.27.690951). This is the closest prior art to our RAG idea.
  - Runs Louvain at resolutions 0.1 to 0.7 and queries GPT-5 ten times per resolution with the top-10 Wilcoxon markers per cluster.
  - Maps the answers to Cell Ontology terms and scores each resolution by consistency, robustness and mean ontology distance. It picks the highest composite score.
  - Evaluated on 12 datasets with a weighted Cell Ontology agreement score. The chosen resolution was best in 8 of 12 and within 10% otherwise.
  - Gaps: no statistical null, no marker splitting, a coarse resolution grid, and a closed-source LLM.
- **HypoGeneAgent** (Yuan et al., Genentech; arXiv Sept 2025; https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.09740). The LLM proposes GO hypotheses for gene-program clusters. Resolution is scored by how similar hypotheses are within a cluster versus between clusters, beating silhouette and modularity on one K562 Perturb-seq dataset.
- **scMRMA** (*Nucleic Acids Research* 2022, 50(2):e7; https://academic.oup.com/nar/article/50/2/e7/6396893). Uses the hierarchical PanglaoDB marker database to drive iterative re-clustering. Authors not re-verified.
- **LLM annotators with split or merge ability, none of which selects resolution in a principled way**
  - GPTCelltype: Hou and Ji, *Nature Methods* 2024 (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-024-02235-4).
  - CASSIA (includes a Subclustering agent): Xie et al., *Nature Communications* 2025 (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-67084-x). Volume and year UNVERIFIED.
  - LICT (checks marker expression to judge credibility): *Communications Biology* 2025 (https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-025-08745-x).
  - CellTypeAgent (verifies against CELLxGENE): arXiv 2025 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.08844).
  - mLLMCelltype (consensus across several LLMs): *Communications Biology* 2026 (https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-026-10420-8).
  - scExtract (reads the source article to annotate; I found no evidence it sets resolution): *Genome Biology* 2025, 26:174 (https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-025-03639-x).
- **scLLM-DSC** (arXiv June 2026; https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13007) injects LLM and NCBI gene embeddings into deep clustering. It does not choose K.

### 7. Clustering benchmarks, and where MI-based methods stand
- **Yu, Cao, Yang, Yang** (*Genome Biology* 2022; https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-022-02622-0). Tested 14 methods on estimating the number of cell types using Tabula Muris subsamples. Monocle3, scLCA, scCCESS-SIMLR, CIDR and Seurat had the best concordance.
- ***Briefings in Bioinformatics* 2024, 25(1):bbad497** (https://academic.oup.com/bib/article/25/1/bbad497/7505072). Seven methods: CosTaL, Seurat, DESC and SC3 beat SCCAF and scDeepCluster.
- ***Genome Biology* 2025** (https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-025-03719-y). 28 methods on 10 paired transcriptomic and proteomic datasets. Top three for transcriptomics were scDCC, scAIDE and FlowSOM. Authors not verified.
- **scCluBench** (arXiv Dec 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.02471; listed in the AAAI-26 proceedings, https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/37110).
  - 15 methods on 36 datasets, run with the true K given.
  - Single-cell foundation models underperformed. Top methods were scCDCG, scMAE and scNAME.
  - scCDCG may come from the same group (UNVERIFIED).
- **arXiv July 2026** (https://arxiv.org/html/2607.25288v1). Deep autoencoders were not significantly better than PCA+Leiden or scVI.
- **MI-based methods:** none of the benchmarks above includes MICA or scMINER, and I found no independent benchmark that does. In scMINER's own evaluation:
  - The 2023 preprint (https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2023.01.26.523391) compared against Seurat, Scanpy and SC3 on 11 datasets using ARI.
  - The published *Nature Communications* 2025, 16:4305 version reportedly used 10 datasets against Seurat, Scanpy, SC3s, scVI and scDeepCluster, adding AMI, NMI, ASW and AvgBIO. This comes from search snippets because the full text was blocked; only partly verified.
  - In the preprint, resolutions for MICA and Seurat were tuned so the number of clusters matched the known number of cell types.
  - Silhouette of 2D UMAP against reference labels was offered as evidence of purity.
  - K is chosen by ranking silhouette plus the user's prior knowledge. The authors call choosing K "a manual and problem-dependent task." I have not checked whether the published version changed this.

---

### GAP ANALYSIS

**Open gaps that look defensible for a publication**
1. **No significance-calibrated resolution selection for MI-distance clustering.** CHOIR, sc-SHC and recall all assume PCA/Euclidean pipelines. A feasible contribution: run CHOIR-style permutation tests or recall-style knockoff genes on MICA's graph mode, then compare against silhouette-based K. This runs on CPU and fits the 120-core machine.
2. **LLM and knowledge-guided resolution choice has a double-dipping problem nobody addresses.** GPTAnno, CASSIA and LICT all feed markers computed on the clusters being judged. Proposed approach:
   - Cluster on the count-split training fold.
   - Derive markers on the test fold.
   - Retrieve evidence from CellMarker, PanglaoDB, the Cell Ontology and literature (RAG).
   - Accept a split only when both the statistical test and the retrieved evidence support it.
   - Evaluate with LCAD or hierarchy-weighted metrics, rare-type F1 and AMI.
   
   This fits Utshab's retrieval and vLLM background, and a local open-weight LLM avoids API cost. I found nothing combining count splitting with LLM annotation.
3. **Evaluation protocol gap.** Benchmarks usually give methods the true K (scCluBench, scMINER). No study evaluates methods at their own automatically selected K using hierarchy-aware plus rare-type metrics. That would be a solid course deliverable and a possible workshop or short paper.
4. **Scale.** Pairwise MI costs O(n^2). Dataset 2 (2M cells) needs graph mode or sketching. CHOIR's 3.3M-cell run is a useful precedent.
5. **Risk.** GPTAnno already occupies "LLM picks resolution via ontology distance." Novelty has to come from statistical calibration, retrieval grounding and MI clustering, not from LLM resolution selection itself.

- No paper with the exact "clustering deserves more attention" title. The closest critiques are CHOIR, sc-SHC, and "From Cluster to Claim" (*Advanced Genetics* 2026, https://doi.org/10.1002/ggn2.70045). The last was blocked (403) and is known only from a search snippet.

**LLM and retrieval-augmented cluster interpretation and cell type annotation, 2023 to 2026 (sweep done 2026-09-16)**

**How I checked the sources.** Nature, Springer and Genome Biology blocked automated fetches, so several numbers come from the PMC or bioRxiv copies of the same papers. Numbers in a published version may differ. The automatic page summaries were unreliable in at least one case. For CellMaster the summary said the tool uses RAG, and the PDF does not support that. So I read the full PDFs for CellMaster, GATHER and HypoGeneAgent myself. The web search budget ran out near the end, so a few items stay UNVERIFIED and are listed at the bottom.

## 1. Main methods found

**Prompting one LLM with a marker list**
- **GPTCelltype.** Hou and Ji, *Nature Methods* 21:1462 (2024), doi:10.1038/s41592-024-02235-4 (full text: PMC11310073).
  - GPT-4 gets the top 10 Wilcoxon DEGs for each cluster. Tested on 10 datasets across 5 species.
  - Labels fully or partially matched the manual labels for over 75% of cell types in most studies. Scoring was full match 1, partial 0.5, mismatch 0, using Cell Ontology (CL) names.
  - It gave the same answer for the same input 85% of the time. The paper warns about hallucination and about the unknown training corpus.
- **DeepCellSeek benchmark.** Xiao et al., *Briefings in Bioinformatics* 26(6):bbaf677 (2025), https://academic.oup.com/bib/article/26/6/bbaf677/8380197.
  - 11 API models on 34 datasets. Perfect match on broad types: Kimi-K2 83.5%, GPT-5 80.6%. SingleR, ScType and CellMarker2.0 were all under 20%.
  - The top 30 genes ranked by p-value plus log2FC beat the top 10. Broad types held up with 60% marker contamination. Subtypes did not.

**Consensus across several LLMs**
- **LICT.** *Communications Biology* (2025), doi:10.1038/s42003-025-08745-x (preprint arXiv:2409.15678).
  - Uses GPT-4, Claude 3 Opus, Gemini 1.5 Pro, ERNIE 4.0 and Llama-3-70B, plus a "talk-to-machine" retry loop.
  - Credibility rule: a label counts as reliable if more than four of the markers the LLM proposed are expressed in at least 80% of the cluster's cells.
- **mLLMCelltype.** bioRxiv (2025), doi:10.1101/2025.04.10.647852.
  - The models deliberate over several rounds. It scored 77.3% against 61.3% for GPTCelltype across 50 datasets.
  - Clusters with low agreement or high entropy are flagged. It has no RAG. The authors list RAG as future work.
- **AnnDictionary.** *Nature Communications* 16:9511 (2025), doi:10.1038/s41467-025-64511-x (preprint bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.10.10.617605).
  - 15 models on Tabula Sapiens v2, with Leiden resolution fixed at 0.5.
  - Claude 3.5 Sonnet reached 84.0% agreement (kappa 0.72). Agreement was judged by an LLM that was never checked against humans. Accuracy tracked model size.

**Multi-agent pipelines**
- **CASSIA.** *Nature Communications* (2025), doi:10.1038/s41467-025-67084-x (preprint bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.12.04.626476).
  - Agents: annotator, validator, scorer and reporter. Optional agents: Annotation Boost, Subclustering, and a RAG agent that queries CellMarker2.0 and ontologies (according to the preprint).
  - Scores are hierarchical on CL, covering 970+ cell types.
- **CellTypeAgent.** arXiv:2505.08844 (2025). The LLM proposes candidate types. The final label is the candidate whose markers have the highest mean expression in CZ CELLxGENE. Tested on 9 datasets, 303 cell types and 36 tissues.
- **CyteType.** bioRxiv (2025), doi:10.1101/2025.11.06.686964. Competing hypotheses are checked against CL, PubMed and marker databases, with pathway enrichment. It reports confidence scores and heterogeneity flags. Details are only partly verified.
- **scExtract.** *Genome Biology* (2025), doi:10.1186/s13059-025-03639-x. It reads the source paper to guide processing and annotation, then uses the labels as priors for integration (scanorama-prior, cellhint-prior).
- **GPTBioInsightor.** *Bioinformatics Advances* 6(1):vbag025 (2026), PMC12975716. The LLM input is DEGs plus pathway enrichment computed with GSEApy.
- **scPilot.** arXiv:2602.11609 (2026). Annotation, trajectory and TF-target tasks on its own scBench.
- **CellMaster.** arXiv:2602.13346 (2026). Detailed under Q2.
- **General agents.**
  - CellAgent: arXiv:2407.09811, ICLR 2026 poster.
  - Biomni: bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.05.30.656746 (2025). Its eight test scenarios include single-cell annotation.
  - CellVoyager: *Nature Methods* 23:749 (2026), doi:10.1038/s41592-026-03029-6. It does open-ended reanalysis, not annotation.
  - BioDiscoveryAgent: ICLR 2025, arXiv:2405.17631. It designs perturbation experiments with PubMed search and does not annotate cells.

**Methods grounded in retrieval or knowledge graphs**
- **GeneAgent.** *Nature Methods* 22 (2025), doi:10.1038/s41592-025-02748-6, PMC12328209. It explains gene sets, not cell types. It checks its own claims against 18 databases.
- **scRAG.** *Findings of ACL* 2025, https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-acl.53/. Uses a tissue-to-cell-type graph and a gene-to-cell-type graph, retrieves similar reference cells, then refines with markers.
- **ReCellTy.** arXiv:2505.00017 and bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.04.23.650201 (2025). GraphRAG in Neo4j over a graph built from CellMarker2.0. GPT-4o-mini rose from 0.50 to 0.67 on a human-scored Azimuth set.
- **scHilda.** *PLoS Computational Biology* 22(5):e1014291 (2026), PMC13175463. Knowledge graph from CL, GO, Reactome and MSigDB. It beat GPTCelltype by 0.049 and CellTypeAgent by 0.038 in agreement score.
- **GATHER.** SIGIR 2026, doi:10.1145/3805712.3809935, arXiv:2605.06403. Walks a 20-database knowledge graph from all input genes at once, weights genes IDF-style, and returns the nodes many genes converge on as evidence.
  - Exact match was 27.45% on Immune (34 fine types) and 59.64% on Tabula Sapiens lung. It used one GPT-4o-mini call per cell and beat the graph-reasoning RAG baselines ToG, ToG-2, RoG and PoG.
- **CellTypeAI.** *Bioinformatics* (2026), PMC13501282. Local models with a hand-built JSON marker file used as RAG.
- **scMarkerAgent.** Research Square rs-9224570 (2026). 890k marker statements mined from 294k PMC full texts, each with a supporting sentence.
- **MAT-Cell.** arXiv:2604.06269 (2026). Adaptive RAG plus verifier agents that debate over reasoning trees.
- **RAGCell.** arXiv:2609.14147, posted 12 Sep 2026. Uses retrieved LLM text embeddings as a training signal for a small encoder.

**Foundation models and embedding methods**

## Q1. Does any method use regulatory network or driver/TF activity as the query or evidence?

**No method I found does this.** Every annotation method above sends marker genes or DEGs to the LLM or the retriever. A few add other signals:
- **Pathway enrichment:** GPTBioInsightor and CyteType.
- **Full DE statistics:** CASSIA Annotation Boost.
- **Filtered marker lists:** LLM-scCurator (bioRxiv 10.64898/2025.12.28.696778) and CELLIA (*BioData Mining* 19:76, 2026, doi:10.1186/s13040-026-00593-7).

The nearest cases:
- **scPilot** gives the LLM pySCENIC TF-gene pairs, but only for a separate task: deciding whether a TF regulates a gene. Its annotation task still uses the top 10 markers.
- **CellMaster's** rationales sometimes cite regulators (for example, IRF8 for pDC). That comes from the LLM's own knowledge, not from a computed activity score.
- **GeneAgent** includes Transfac among its verification databases, but it explains gene sets, not clusters.
- **EpiAgent** (*Nature Methods* 22:2316, 2025, doi:10.1038/s41592-025-02822-z) is a scATAC foundation model, not an LLM agent.

I found nothing that feeds SCENIC AUCell, VIPER/metaVIPER, DoRothEA/decoupleR, or NetBID/scMINER driver activity into an LLM or retriever as evidence. That includes "hidden drivers" with little differential expression. This is exactly the output scMINER produces.

## Q2. Does any method feed the LLM verdict back into the clustering?

Yes, a few do. This is the most crowded part of your planned contribution.
- **GPTAnno.** Song, ..., Hou, bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.11.27.690951 (2025), PMC12687786. It is from the GPTCelltype author's lab.
  - Runs clustering at resolutions 0.1 to 0.7 in steps of 0.2 and queries GPT-5 repeatedly for each cluster.
  - Maps the answers to CL and scores each resolution on consistency, robustness and dispersion on the ontology tree. It picks the resolution with the best combined score.
  - It favours coarse resolutions, then subclusters hierarchically. No open-weight models were tested.
- **HypoGeneAgent.** Genentech, arXiv:2509.09740 (2025).
  - Leiden at resolutions 0.1 to 1.0 on K562 CRISPRi Perturb-seq data.
  - GPT-o3 retrieves from GO, KEGG and PubMed and proposes up to 5 GO hypotheses for each cluster.
  - The resolution score combines agreement among a cluster's hypotheses (ICS, weight 1/3) with how different the top hypothesis is from those of other clusters (1 − ICD, weight 2/3), using text embeddings.
  - It calls itself "the first framework that closes the loop." It targets GO programs, not cell types, and the paper calls itself a preliminary test.
- **CellMaster.** arXiv:2602.13346 (2026).
  - Each loop outputs a label, a confidence score and a recommended next step (split/merge, finer markers, zoom-in). Zoom-in reclusters the chosen clusters at resolution 0.1 to 2.0.
  - A human accepts the suggestions. Average score was 0.602 across 9 datasets, +0.071 over the best baseline. Human feedback added +0.115.
- **Tools that only flag clusters:** mLLMCelltype, LICT, CyteType (heterogeneity) and CASSIA (its subclustering agent annotates subclusters the user supplies).
- **CLUEY.** bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.11.14.623697 (2024). It picks the number of clusters recursively by correlating clusters with atlas cell-type profiles. It uses no LLM, but it is a natural baseline.

I found no work that:
- merges or splits pairs of clusters based on retrieval-grounded label equivalence,
- works with mutual-information clustering, or
- scores the resulting partitions with ARI/NMI against over-clustered baselines. I could not confirm whether GPTAnno reports ARI.

## 0. Bottom line

- MICA uses no new clustering algorithm. It computes a binned mutual information (MI) distance between cells over all genes. It then runs either classical MDS plus k-means (under 5,000 cells) or an HNSW MI-kNN graph, node2vec, a Euclidean kNN graph and Louvain (5,000 cells or more). Reviewer #2 wrote that the paper "does not propose fundamentally new methods" (Peer Review File).
- The accuracy numbers use an oracle. In MDS mode k was set to the true number of classes. For MICA-GE and the baselines, resolution was swept from 0.1 to 4 until the cluster count matched the truth, keeping the highest ARI.
- The largest run was Covid650K (647,366 cells): 13 h and 204.4 GB peak on 40 CPU cores. MICA has no GPU path.
- The `main` code would not run 2M cells as shipped. It densifies an n×n kNN adjacency, which is about 32 TB at n=2M. Even the sparse branches would likely take over 12 h and use 450 to 650 GB (estimate).
- I found no 2025 or 2026 paper that extends MICA's clustering itself. The citing papers apply the network and activity side, extend it (APNet, lncAPNet), or cite it in reviews and new clustering methods.

## 1. MICA clustering pipeline

### 1.1 Preprocessing (scMINER R side)
- **QC.** Metrics are nUMI, nFeature, pctMito (`MT-|mt-`), pctSpikeIn (`ERCC-`) and per-gene nCell. The "auto" cutoffs are Median ± 3×MAD (`drawSparseEsetQC()`, `filterSparseEset()`).
- **Normalization.** Counts go to CPM and then log2 (`normalizeSparseEset()`). TPM datasets were only log2-transformed.
- **No feature selection.** MICA uses all genes that pass QC, and the paper argues against HVG selection.
- **Export.** `generateMICAinput()` writes .txt or .h5ad. It first calls `as.matrix()`, which makes the matrix dense in R, and it has an optional `downSample_N`.

### 1.2 How MI between two cells is estimated
Source: Methods Eq. 1 to 3, plus `MICA/lib/distance.py`, `MICA/lib/mutual_info.py` and `mihnsw/hnswlib/space_mi.h`.
- **What the samples are.** Each cell is a vector over G genes. The MI between cells i and j treats the G genes as paired samples of two discrete variables.
- **Binning.** Bins are equal-width, computed separately for each cell between its own min and max expression. The number of bins is b = floor(G^(1/3)), so 20,000 genes give 27 bins. The flags `-bsz` (fixed b) and `-bpr` (power) override this.
- **Estimator.** A plug-in estimate from the 2D histogram, with no bias correction and no explicit handling of zeros.
- **Speed.** The GE path runs in a C++ HNSW fork ("mihnsw") with a custom `space='mi'`. The MDS path is a pure-Python double loop over `np.histogram2d` (`mi_calc`) and is effectively single-threaded.

### 1.3 MI to distance
- **Paper (Eq. 3).** D = 1 − I(Ci;Cj)/H(Ci,Cj). This matches the C++ HNSW code, which computes `2 − (hx+hy)/hxy`, and the numba distance.
- **Discrepancy.** In the MDS path of v1.0.0 and `main`, `mi_norm` computes D = 1 − I/sqrt(H_i·H_j) instead. That is a different normalization from the one in the paper. This comes from my reading of the code and was not tested.

### 1.4 MICA-MDS (small data)
- **Steps.** The full n×n MI distance matrix goes into classical MDS: double-centering, `np.linalg.eigh`, then keep the positive eigenvalues (`transform.py`). The first 19 dimensions are kept by default, and the paper says ARI plateaus from about 5 dimensions (Fig. 2f,g). k-means runs on that embedding.
- **Consensus.** The paper says k-means runs 10 times and the runs are combined by consensus clustering. In the v1.0.0 code the default is a single `sklearn.KMeans(n_clusters=k)`. With sklearn 0.24.1 that means n_init=10 and the best inertia is kept, which is not consensus.
  - A consensus over several `-dd` dimension values (co-association matrix plus average-linkage hierarchical clustering) was added on 2025-03-31 (commit dfe3ddc0).
  - The legacy 0.2.x code did SC3-style consensus over dimensions and bootstraps.
- **Choosing k.** The user must supply k (`-nck`, default 4). A multi-k option was added in 2024. The wrapper suggests `-nck 4 5 6 7 8 9 10 -dd 20`, and an optional silhouette score (`-sil`) can help pick among them.

### 1.5 MICA-GE (large data), `mica_ge.py` defaults
1. Approximate kNN graph under the MI distance with HNSW: k=80 (`-nnm`), ef=400, M=8.
2. node2vec through pecanpy (SparseOTF, weighted): 20 dimensions, walk length 60, 110 walks per node, window 10, p=2.8, q=0.4.
3. Exact kNN on the 20-D embedding (sklearn ball_tree, k=20, Euclidean or cosine).
4. Louvain with python-louvain (`community.best_partition`). Default resolution is 1.822, and a range can be swept in parallel (`-minr/-maxr/-ss`, `-nw` workers).
5. Optional consensus (`-cs CSPA`), off by default.
6. UMAP (min_dist 0.6) or t-SNE for display.

The mode switch is in `mica auto`: GE when cells ≥ `-cc` (5,000), MDS otherwise. The authors call the 5,000 threshold "an empirical guideline rather than a strict cutoff" (Peer Review File).

### 1.6 Two things I inferred from the code (not tested)
- **Distances used as weights.** In GE, MI distances are written as edge weights for weighted node2vec, and `kneighbors_graph(mode='distance')` feeds Euclidean distances to Louvain as weights. Farther neighbors therefore get larger weights. The effect on accuracy is not measured anywhere.
- **Dense adjacency.** Both `main` and tag 1.0.0 run `kneighbors_graph(...).toarray()` and then `nx.from_numpy_matrix`, which builds a dense n×n matrix. At 650K cells that is about 3.4 TB. It cannot be the code that produced the published 153 to 204 GB Covid650K run.
  - Branches `huge_dataset` and `huge_floating_k` (Dec 2024 to Jan 2025) switch to sparse matrices and float32. PR #29 was closed and PR #30 is still open.
  - So the exact code behind the large benchmark is UNVERIFIED.

## 2. SJARACNe networks and NetBID-style activity and hidden drivers

**Per-cluster network inputs** (`generateSJARACNeInput()`)
- One folder per group (a cluster or an annotated cell type). Each folder holds an expression file (genes × cells) plus hub lists.
- Hub lists are curated: about 1,500 TFs and more than 5,500 signaling genes (SIGs) for human or mouse (`inst/RData/tf_sigs_*.RData`). In the PBMC14K demo, the B-cell group had 835 TFs and 4,148 SIGs present among 8,572 genes.
- Default `downSample_N = 1000` cells per group. Optional SuperCell metacells: the paper used gamma=20 for benchmarks and superCell_gamma=50 for activity clustering.
- The code warns below 100 single cells or 50 metacells per group. The Discussion states a minimum of 500 cells overall.

**SJARACNe algorithm** (Methods, and Khatamian A et al., Bioinformatics 2019, https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/bty907)
1. Gene-gene MI by adaptive partitioning, as in ARACNe-AP (Lachmann A et al., Bioinformatics 2016, https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btw216).
2. Edges filtered at `-pb` 1e-7, then Data Processing Inequality pruning.
3. `-n 100` bootstraps and a consensus network kept at `-pc`. The cutoff is 1e-2 for single cells, 1e-3 for metacells and 1e-5 for bulk data (docs).
4. Edges are annotated with Spearman and Pearson correlation, slope and p-value, and each target is signed.
- It runs as a C++ core behind a Python and CWL wrapper, locally with cwltool (needs node.js) or on LSF with cwlexec.

**Activity** (`getActivity_individual` and `getActivity_inBatch`)
- Expression is z-normalized per column. Activity is then the mean of each driver's targets.
- Methods: "mean" (default), "weightedmean" (MI × sign of Spearman, which is the NetBID2 default), "absmean" and "maxmean".
- Per-cluster activity matrices are concatenated, and missing values are filled with the minimum non-NA value.
- **Hidden drivers** are drivers that change in differential activity (`getDA()`, default t-test, with limma and Wilcoxon also available) but not in expression.
- scMINER does not use NetBID2's Bayesian BID model (Dong X et al., Nat Commun 14:2581, 2023, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-38335-6).

**Compute cost (not reported in the paper)**
- Work scales with hubs × genes × bootstraps, and each adaptive-partitioning MI costs about O(m log m) for m cells.
- The PBMC14K demo LSF script reserves 8 GB and 1 slot.
- Users report much more:
  - A 2025 comment on SJARACNe issue #50 says 1,361 cells on 32 cores needed 160 to 200 GB.
  - A ~300K-cell run failed with SIGTERM, and the maintainers' answer was to downsample.
  - A 2019 maintainer note (issue #3) puts 28K genes × 1,000 samples at about 8 GB.
- **Calibration problem (new, unmerged).** Draft PR #73 (Aug 2026, developer "adamdingliang") argues the legacy consensus p-value uses an uncorrected normal tail. On BRCA100 it understates the tail about 94-fold for TF and 452-fold for SIG networks. The PR proposes a fixed minimum-recurrence rule (K_edge=6), and PR #71 adds estimator-matched null models. This shows the default `-pc` threshold is not a calibrated p-value.

## 3. Complexity, runtime, memory, and 2M-cell feasibility

**Asymptotics (my analysis of the code)**
- **MDS mode.** O(n²·G) MI evaluations, O(n²) memory and an O(n³) eigendecomposition.
- **GE mode.** About O(n log n) HNSW distance calls, each O(G + b²). On top of that come the random-walk tokens (n × 110 × 60), a kNN graph on the 20-D embedding, and one Louvain run per resolution in the sweep.

**Would it run on 2,000,000 cells on the project server? Not as shipped. Probably not within 12 h even after fixes. All figures below are estimates.**
1. **`main` or v1.0.0.** The dense `.toarray()` on the final kNN graph needs about 2e6² × 8 bytes, or 32 TB. It fails at once. The R export `as.matrix()` for 2M × 20K genes needs about 320 GB and writes a huge text file.

3. **Workable options.**

## 6. Limitations

**Stated in the Discussion**
1. It needs at least 500 cells, which limits rare-population studies. Suggested workarounds are signal amplification (computational or experimental) or mapping to references such as the Human Cell Atlas.
2. Activity is only estimated for the curated TF and SIG lists, so new non-TF, non-SIG drivers are missed. The proposed future work is to use both upstream and downstream first-order neighbors.
3. There is no ground truth for large datasets, so the accuracy benchmark covers only small datasets.
- The reviewers also raised the unclear rationale for the mode split and how to pick resolution without labels. The authors answered with resolution sweeps, silhouette scores and marker inspection. The docs pick PBMC14K resolution 2.05 "based on the knowledge about" the dataset.

**Inferred (from code and design, not tested)**
- **Dropout and zeros.** Equal-width per-cell bins put zeros and low values in bin 0, so the (0,0) cell of the joint histogram dominates. MI then largely reflects co-detection patterns and sequencing depth. There is no dropout model or bias correction, and MI between cells ignores gene identity beyond pairing.
- **Low-dimensional data breaks the estimator.** With p=10 or 20 features, b = floor(p^(1/3)) = 2 bins, and MI is estimated from 10 to 20 samples. That is close to meaningless. MICA's cell-to-cell MI only makes sense for high-dimensional data such as Dataset 3. Datasets 1 and 2 would need an MI over features instead.
- **Cost.** MDS mode is quadratic in time and memory with a cubic eigensolve. Both modes keep the whole matrix dense and use all genes.
- **Resolution and k.** There is no automatic model selection, and published accuracy depends on oracle k or resolution. python-louvain can produce badly connected communities, which Leiden fixes (Traag VA et al., Sci Rep 2019, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-019-41695-z).
- **Weights, seeds, batches.** Distances are used as weights (section 1.6). No random seeds are set for KMeans, Louvain, HNSW or walks. Harmony batch correction is commented out as "does not work well".
- **SJARACNe cutoff.** The consensus threshold is miscalibrated, per the developers' own PR #73.

## 1. How trustworthy the labels are

From most to least trustworthy:
1. Labels from genotype demultiplexing (Tahoe-100M, CellBench) or from the experimental design, such as culture condition (Kolodziejczyk).
2. FACS sorting (Zheng sorted PBMC).
3. Manual gating (cytometry).
4. Curated labels made by clustering the same data (Allen atlas, Zeisel, Baron, Parse). These are circular: they favor methods that work like the one used to make them.
5. Label transfer (HLCA extended, MERFISH mapped to the 10x taxonomy).

The report should state which tier each dataset's labels come from.

  | 20% | 6.4 GB |
  | 50% | 16 GB, same as dense |

  int32 indices work up to 2^31 nonzeros, which is about 54% density here. The densities for HVG matrices are estimates, not measured.
- **Full matrix before HVG selection** (Allen 10Xv3, 2.3M × 32K genes):
  - Assuming about 3,000 detected genes per cell (UNVERIFIED), that is about 7e9 nonzeros. That exceeds the int32 limit, so indices go to int64 at 12 B per nonzero, about **84 GB**.

  - 50 PCs: 0.4 GB.
  - kNN graph with k=15: 30M edges, well under 1 GB.
  - k-means distance buffer at K=338 subclasses: 2.7 GB.
  - All fine on GPU.
- **Hard limit:** Any method that needs an n × n matrix is impossible at 2M cells: pairwise distances, pairwise MI, SC3-style consensus, dense spectral or agglomerative clustering. That matrix is 4e12 × 4 B = **16 TB**. Even 100K × 100K is 40 GB.
  - This is why MICA switches to graph mode above 5,000 cells.
  - Computing MI from each cell to m landmark cells costs n × m. At m = 2,000 that is 16 GB, which is feasible and could be a scalable-scMINER angle to explore.

# Literature sweep: MI-based similarity and million-cell clustering (as of 2026-09-16)

## 0. What scMINER/MICA actually computes (checked against the paper and the code)

- **Paper:** Pan et al., Nat Commun 2025, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59620-6. The cell-cell distance is D = 1 − I(Ci;Cj)/H(Ci,Cj). Genes are the samples. Expression is put into equal-width bins, with b = n_genes^(1/3) bins. MICA-MDS (≤5,000 cells) builds the full MI matrix, runs MDS to 19 dims, then consensus k-means. MICA-GE (>5,000 cells) builds an MI kNN graph (k=80), runs node2vec to 20 dims, builds a Euclidean kNN graph (k=20) and runs Louvain.
- **Accuracy evidence is small-scale only.** The ARI benchmark uses 10 small ground-truth datasets (mean ARI 0.84). MI was compared with Pearson, Spearman and Euclidean on only 4 gold-standard sets (Yan, Pollen, Kolod, Buettner).
  - HMC76K, Covid97K and Covid650K were used for runtime and memory only, on a 40-core CPU. The numbers are only in Supplementary Fig. 4c.
  - The authors admit this: "absence of ground-truth datasets for large-scale datasets limits the accuracy benchmark". They also state that scMINER "requires a minimum of 500 cells".
- **The code differs from the paper** (github.com/jyyulab/MICA, master).
  - The Methods say HNSW (hnswlib). `MICA/mica_ge.py` actually calls `pynndescent.NNDescent(metric=numba_calc_mi_dis, n_neighbors=80)`.
  - `requirements.txt` pins pynndescent 0.5.2 and has no hnswlib. Dependencies are 2021-era (numpy 1.20).
  - The graph is built in networkx and clustered with python-louvain. At millions of cells these are likely bottlenecks (my inference, UNVERIFIED).
- **D is a true metric.** 1 − I/H(X,Y) is the normalized variation of information. Vinh, Epps & Bailey prove it is a metric (JMLR 2010, Theorem 3, https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume11/vinh10a/vinh10a.pdf). Kraskov et al. state the same (EPL 2005, https://doi.org/10.1209/epl/i2004-10483-y).
  - MICA bins each cell into a partition of the gene set, so D is exactly a metric on those binned cells (a pseudometric on raw cells).
  - This matters for scaling. Triangle-inequality pruning and farthest-first sketching guarantees carry over to MI space.

## 1. Information-theoretic similarity for scRNA-seq

**Benchmarks of similarity metrics**
- **Skinnider, Squair & Foster**, Nat Methods 2019, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-019-0372-4.
  - Tested 17 measures. Proportionality (ρp, φs) was best across tasks.
  - MI (computed with WGCNA) "performed relatively poorly on one or more tasks".
  - Cell clustering was tested on only 561 cells from 7 cell lines.
  - This contradicts scMINER's claim that MI is better, and neither study is at scale.
- **Kim et al.**, Brief Bioinform 2019, https://doi.org/10.1093/bib/bby076. Correlation-based metrics beat distance-based ones. Whether MI was in their panel is UNVERIFIED.
- **Watson et al.**, Brief Bioinform 2022, https://doi.org/10.1093/bib/bbac387. Tested 17 proximity metrics. The best one depends on sparsity, rarity and whether structure is discrete or continuous. Euclidean did poorly. MI was not in their list.
- **Ji et al.**, bioRxiv 2023, https://doi.org/10.1101/2023.12.26.572833. Compares distances between cell populations, not cells. MSE and cosine were best.
- **scCluBench** (Xu et al., arXiv Dec 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.02471). Covers 14 methods and 36 datasets, the largest about 27.5K cells. No MI-based method is included.
- **Yin et al.**, Genome Biol 2025, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-025-03719-y. A clustering benchmark. Details are UNVERIFIED because PMC returned a captcha.

**Information-theoretic distances already run at multi-million scale**
- **minicore** (Baker, Dyjack, Braverman, Hicks, Langmead; bioRxiv 2021, https://doi.org/10.1101/2021.03.24.436859, and ACM BCB 2021).
  - Does k-means++, localsearch++ and mini-batch k-means with JSD, KL and Bhattacharyya on sparse counts.
  - Clusters 4.06M cells in minutes using under 10 GiB RAM.
  - This is the closest prior art for information-theoretic distances at multi-million scale. It treats each cell as a distribution and uses divergences, not MI between profiles.

**MI estimators relevant to sparse counts**
- **Plug-in histogram:** MICA.
- **Adaptive partitioning:** Darbellay & Vajda, IEEE TIT 1999, https://doi.org/10.1109/18.761290. Also ARACNe-AP (Lachmann et al., Bioinformatics 2016, https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btw216), about 200x faster than fixed bandwidth. Also SJARACNe (Khatamian et al., Bioinformatics 2019, https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/bty907).
- **KSG kNN estimator:** Kraskov et al., Phys Rev E 2004, https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevE.69.066138.
  - Mixed discrete-continuous KSG handles point masses at zero: Gao et al., NeurIPS 2017, https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.06212.
  - Normi used mixed KSG specifically against dropouts (Zeng et al., Brief Bioinform 2023, https://doi.org/10.1093/bib/bbad326).
  - Shachaf et al. show kNN-MI beats fixed binning for GRN inference (BMC Bioinformatics 2023, https://doi.org/10.1186/s12859-022-05047-5).
- **MIMIQ** (O'Hanlon et al., bioRxiv 2026, https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.04.10.717770). Adaptive binning built for small integer counts, with a negative-binomial copula χ² test. It is gene-gene only.
- **Other gene-gene MI:** SINUM (BMC Bioinformatics 2024, https://doi.org/10.1186/s12859-024-05895-3) and PIDC (Chan et al., Cell Systems 2017, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cels.2017.08.014).
- **Zero-inflation-aware MI for cell-cell distance:** none found.

**Fast, GPU and approximate MI**
- **CUDA B-spline MI**, up to 82x (Shi et al., BMC Res Notes 2011, https://doi.org/10.1186/1756-0500-4-189).
- **GPU-ARACNE** (He et al., BMC Syst Biol 2017, https://doi.org/10.1186/s12918-017-0458-5).
- **TINGe**, parallel whole-genome MI (Zola et al., IEEE TPDS 2010).
- **GPU joint-histogram MI** for image registration, about 25x (Shams et al., Comput Methods Programs Biomed 2010). This is the same kernel as cell-cell MI (paired vectors into a joint histogram).
- **EDGE** (Noshad, Zeng & Hero, ICASSP 2019, https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.09125). LSH-based MI estimator in O(N) time for one pair of high-dimensional variables.
- **Sliced MI** (Goldfeld & Greenewald, NeurIPS 2021, https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.05279). It has been criticized as saturating and deceptive (Semenenko et al., arXiv 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.04053).
- **Fast-mRMR** (Ramírez-Gallego et al., Int J Intell Syst 2017) covers MI feature selection on CPU, GPU and Spark.
- All of these speed up gene-gene MI or single-pair estimation. None builds a kNN graph over millions of objects under an MI distance.

## 3. Prior work scaling MI distances to millions of objects

I found nothing that computes a pairwise MI distance, or an MI kNN graph, over more than 1M objects in any field. The closest items:

- **MICA-GE at 650K cells.** It uses NN-Descent with an exact per-pair MI, reports runtime only, and has no accuracy check at that size.
- **minicore at 4M cells,** with divergences rather than MI.
- **LSH for f-divergences and "mutual information loss"** (Chen et al., NeurIPS 2019, https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.12414). It hashes distributions, not the MI between two profiles.
- **EDGE,** which is one MI estimate over many samples.
- **Learned embeddings where Euclidean distance mimics an expensive metric** (Courty et al., "Learning Wasserstein Embeddings", ICLR 2018, https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.07457). This is a template for distilling MI distance into a FAISS-searchable space. I found no MI version.
- **No random-projection, sketch or landmark (Nyström) approximation of a cell-cell MI matrix** was found.

## 4. Cluster-then-propagate and rare-population guarantees

**In practice:** Seurat v5 ProjectData (`refdata = list(cluster_full = "seurat_clusters")`), the ABC atlas kNN imputation, and SnapATAC Nyström extension. None of them reports label accuracy on the propagated cells for rare types. The Seurat vignette does not quantify it.

**Theory that exists, all generic:**
- **Uniform sampling.** P(miss a population with fraction p) ≤ exp(−ps). CURE (Guha et al., SIGMOD 1998, https://doi.org/10.1145/276304.276312) gives a Chernoff sample-size bound so that each cluster u gets at least f|u| points with probability 1−δ (Theorem 4.1). The formula is paraphrased from a poorly OCRed PDF, so check it against the original.
- **Farthest-first traversal** is a 2-approximation of the k-center/Hausdorff objective (as used in Hopper). It works in any metric space, including MI space.
- **Kernel herding** converges in MMD (Chen, Welling & Smola, UAI 2010, https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.3472). It preserves proportions, so it does not enrich rare types.
- **Sensitivity-sampling coresets** (e.g. https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.01339) bound k-means cost, not recovery of a specific small cluster.
- **Nyström spectral clustering** is said to lack a bounded approximation ratio (Entropy 2018, https://doi.org/10.3390/e20070519). I did not verify this against the original proof.
- **Leverage scores** favoring rare populations is a heuristic claim (Seurat vignette), not a theorem.

I found no bound connecting sketch size, rare-type fraction, metric and kNN propagation error for single-cell data.

## 5. Gap analysis

**G1. No accuracy evidence for MI clustering above about 10K labeled cells.** scMINER itself reports only efficiency at 650K. Skinnider 2019 found MI weak. So "MI beats Euclidean on PCA at atlas scale, especially for rare types" is untested and could well come out negative. Evaluation targets with deep hierarchical labels already exist: the ABC atlas (about 4M cells) and Cao 2M (used by minicore).

**G2. No sketching or landmarks in MI space.** Every sketcher works in PCA or Euclidean space. Because MICA's D is a proven metric, farthest-first sketching under D inherits Hopper's 2-approximation Hausdorff guarantee in MI geometry. Landmark lower bounds |D(x,l) − D(y,l)| ≤ D(x,y) are also valid for pruning kNN candidates. Neither use was found.

**G3. No GPU cell-cell MI.** GPU MI exists only for gene-gene networks (2011, 2017) and image registration. Two unused ideas:
- A batched joint histogram, using bincount on b·bin_i + bin_j, or a one-hot contingency table computed by matmul.
- Sparsity. The (0,0) cell of the table equals G minus the number of genes with bin > 0 in either cell, so a pair only needs its nonzero high-bin genes.

This is feasible on 2x RTX 6000 Ada, but it is engineering. On its own it is probably not enough for a paper.

**G4. The cell-cell MI estimator has never been examined.**
- MICA uses per-cell min-max equal-width binning with about 20 bins for ~8,000 genes (b = G^(1/3)). With 80-95% zeros, bin 0 dominates and MI mostly reflects co-detection, which likely depends on sequencing depth (UNVERIFIED hypothesis).
- The following have not been compared for cell-cell distances: NVI vs NID (1 − I/max H), adaptive partitioning, mixed KSG, and count-aware binning (MIMIQ-style).
- scMINER only varied bin count (5 to 100).

**G5. No theory for sketch-then-propagate on rare types under a non-Euclidean metric.** CURE, k-center and herding bounds have not been tied to kNN label-propagation error on rare types. A bound plus empirical check (population separation greater than 2× covering radius implies a representative is sampled) looks doable in a semester.

**G6. Reproducibility.** The paper says HNSW but the code uses NN-Descent. Dependencies are pinned to 2021, and there are no accuracy benchmarks at large scale.

**Cost (rough, UNVERIFIED).** NN-Descent with k=80 means roughly 1e10 to 1e11 MI evaluations for 2M cells, each over thousands of genes. Running MICA-GE unmodified at 2M cells is likely many CPU hours to days. Time it on 100K cells first.

**Candidate contribution, stated skeptically.** Farthest-first sketch in MI metric (with guarantee), exact GPU MI on the sketch, clustering, then propagation with landmark pruning, plus the rare-type bound (G2 + G3 + G5). Its value depends entirely on G1 showing MI helps. A careful negative result would still be publishable as a benchmark.

ideas.title: MI-kNN at atlas scale: exact retrieve-then-rerank mutual information graphs for MICA on 2M+ cells
ideas.one_line: Get MICA's graph mode to run on 2M+ cells in under 12 h on one workstation. Each cell is binned once, cheap first-stage retrieval proposes neighbor candidates, and an exact GPU MI kernel reranks them. This gives the first labeled test of whether MI clustering beats PCA-Leiden at atlas scale, especially for rare types.
ideas.problem_and_gap:
(1) MICA's largest published run was Covid650K: 13 h and 204 GB on 40 cores. It was timed but never scored with ARI (Pan et al., Nat Commun 2025, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59620-6, Supp. Fig. 4). The authors' Discussion admits there is no large-scale ground truth.
(2) The shipped code cannot reach 2M cells. The kNN graph is densified (kneighbors_graph(...).toarray(), about 32 TB at 2M), and the R export calls as.matrix(). Even the sparse branches are estimated to take more than 12 h (deep-read estimate).
(3) The pipeline, checked by me on 2026-09-16 on main:
- MICA/mica_ge.py builds the MI kNN graph with hnswlib Index(space='mi') and 80 neighbors, then node2vec (pecanpy) to 20 dims, then Louvain at resolution 1.822.
- MICA/lib/distance.py (numba_calc_mi_dis) uses equal-width bins between each cell's own min and max, and D = 1 - I/H(X,Y).
- The colleague report saying graph mode uses pynndescent does not match main. It may describe another branch (UNVERIFIED).
(4) MDS mode computes histograms pair by pair in Python. Klein (2,717 cells) took 3,112 s, against 43 s for Scanpy.
(5) There is no GPU path. Nobody has built an MI kNN graph over more than 1M objects in any field (scalable-MI report). My Europe PMC query on 2026-09-16 (MI + single-cell + clustering, 2025-2026) found no MICA extension.
(6) Independent evidence that MI is a good cell-cell similarity is thin. Skinnider et al. (Nat Methods 2019, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-019-0372-4) found MI weak, but tested only 561 cells. So accuracy at scale is an open question, and a negative answer would also be publishable.
ideas.method_sketch:
1. Pre-binning. Compute MICA's exact per-cell codes (per-cell min-max bins, b = floor(G^(1/3))) once as uint8, stored sparsely (nonzero bins only), plus each cell's marginal entropy H(X).
- For 10x UMI data after log2(CPM+1), bin 0 holds only zeros: the smallest nonzero, about log2(1e6/UMI + 1), is far above max/b.
- Check this per dataset and fall back to dense codes where it fails.

2. Exact pair kernel. Fill the joint b x b table from the union of nonzero genes, with n00 = G - |S_i U S_j|. Then D = 1 - (H_i + H_j - H_ij)/H_ij.
- Implement as a batched bincount over offsets pair*b^2 + b*ci + cj (PyTorch, CuPy or Triton).
- Unit-test that it matches numba_calc_mi_dis bit for bit on 10K random pairs.

3. Stage-1 candidates (the IR framing). Take the union of the top-C neighbors from:
- (a) FAISS-GPU cosine on 50 PCs of log-CPM;
- (b) MinHash LSH on each cell's set of detected genes (Jaccard). Motivation: co-detection dominates MI.
Use C in {100, 200, 500}.

4. Stage-2 rerank. Compute exact MI distance for every candidate and keep the top k (k = 15 to 80).

5. Certification. NVI = 1 - I/H(X,Y) is a true metric (Vinh, Epps & Bailey, JMLR 2010, https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume11/vinh10a/vinh10a.pdf).
- With m = 256 landmarks, the lower bound max_l |D(x,l) - D(y,l)| proves when a non-candidate cannot enter a cell's kNN list (LAESA-style pivot pruning).
- Report the fraction of cells whose kNN list is certified exact.

6. Clustering. Run Leiden directly on the MI-kNN graph with similarity weights (1 - D). Compare against MICA's node2vec, then Euclidean kNN, then Louvain. Ablate the distance-used-as-weight choice found in the MICA code.

7. Comparison arm. Farthest-first sketch in the NVI metric (Hopper-style 2-approximation covering guarantee; DeMeo & Berger, Bioinformatics 2020, https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa408), then exact MI clustering on the sketch, then kNN label propagation.
ideas.experiments:
D1 (>=5K samples, >=20 vars)
- PBMC14K: 13,605 cells x 17,986 genes, FACS labels, ships with scMINER.
- Exactness against MICA: distances equal, recall of MICA's HNSW graph, ARI at MICA's documented resolution.
- Optional: the full Zheng 2017 sorted collection (about 94K cells, count UNVERIFIED).
- Caveat: PBMC14K is high-dimensional. If the instructor wants a low-dimensional D1, use Levine_32dim, but MI over 32 features is weak (see Idea 2).

D2 (>=2M samples, >=10 vars)
- Allen whole mouse brain 10Xv3: 2.3M cells x 32,285 genes, public S3, CC BY-NC 4.0. Labels at class (34), subclass (338) and supertype (1,201) levels (Yao et al., Nature 2023, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06812-z).
- Allen labels came from a PCA-style Leiden pipeline, which biases toward the baselines. As a non-circular check, add a 2M-cell slice of Tahoe-100M (CC0, cell-line labels from demuxlet; https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.02.20.639398).

D3 (>=500 samples, >=700 vars)
- Zeisel 2015 (3,005 x 19,972; 9- and 47-level labels), Klein, Usoskin and Kolodziejczyk.
- Run exact all-pairs GPU MI for MDS mode, reproduce scMINER's ARIs, and report the speedup over 3,112 s on Klein.

Baselines
- MICA-GE on 100K and 300K subsamples (the full set is infeasible).
- rapids-singlecell PCA+Leiden (https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02402).
- scVI+Leiden, SC3s, Seurat v5 sketch + ProjectData (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-023-01767-y).
- minicore JSD k-means (https://doi.org/10.1101/2021.03.24.436859).

Metrics
- recall@k against brute-force exact MI kNN on 20K-cell subsets;
- wall time and peak RAM/VRAM;
- ARI and AMI at matched K and at auto-selected resolution;
- hierarchy-aware wNMI (Wu & Wu, Genome Biol 2020, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-020-02027-x);
- F1 for rare subclasses (under 0.1% of cells);
- certified-exact fraction.

Ablations: candidate source (PCA, MinHash, union), C, all genes vs 2K/5K HVGs, node2vec vs direct Leiden, weight semantics, k.
ideas.compute_estimate:
All figures are UNVERIFIED estimates until a prototype runs.
- Pre-binning 2.3M cells from about 84 GB of sparse CSR on CPU: under 1 h.
- Candidates: FAISS-GPU on 2.3M x 50 dims takes minutes. MinHash on 120 cores takes under 1 h.
- Rerank: 2.3M x 200 = 4.6e8 pairs. At about 4K to 6K genes in each pair's nonzero union, that is about 2.5e12 element operations, roughly 1 to 3 GPU-hours spread over 2 GPUs.
- Landmarks: 2.3M x 256 = 5.9e8 pairs, the same order.
- Leiden on about 35M edges: minutes on GPU, or under 1 h with igraph on CPU.
- Brute-force exact kNN on 20K-cell subsets: 2e8 pairs each, under 1 h.
- Target: the full D2 pipeline in under 8 h, inside one 12 h window.
- Memory: about 150 to 250 GB peak host RAM, under 40 GB per GPU with batching.
- No model training. Everything else (D1, D3, baselines on subsamples) runs overnight.
ideas.novelty_claim:
Two claims.
1. The first exact kNN graph under the cell-cell MI distance at 2M or more cells on a single workstation, with recall measured against brute force and a metric-based certificate of exactness.
2. The first labeled accuracy evaluation of MI-distance clustering at atlas scale, including rare types and hierarchical labels.

What a reviewer would search for: GPU cell-cell MI, MI kNN over more than 1M objects, and any MICA scalability follow-up. None were found in the two colleague reports or in my Europe PMC check of 2025-2026 MI + single-cell clustering papers (2026-09-16).
ideas.closest_prior_work:
- MICA-GE itself: 650K cells, timing only (Pan et al. 2025).
- minicore: 4M cells with JSD/KL k-means, which uses divergences rather than MI (Baker et al., bioRxiv 2021 / ACM BCB 2021, https://doi.org/10.1101/2021.03.24.436859).
- rapids-singlecell (arXiv 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02402).
- GPU-ARACNE, gene-gene MI only (He et al., BMC Syst Biol 2017, https://doi.org/10.1186/s12918-017-0458-5).
- Hopper farthest-first sketching (Bioinformatics 2020).
- Seurat v5 sketching (Hao et al., Nat Biotechnol 2024).
- SC3s (BMC Bioinformatics 2022, https://doi.org/10.1186/s12859-022-05085-z).
- FAISS (arXiv 2401.08281) and CAGRA (ICDE 2024, arXiv 2308.15136), which support only L2 and inner-product metrics.
ideas.risks:
- MI may not beat PCA-Leiden or scVI at 2M. Then this becomes an honest benchmark, which is publishable but at a lower venue.
- Reviewers may call it engineering. The certification and the accuracy-at-scale study have to carry the science.
- Candidate recall may be low if MI neighbors differ from PCA neighbors. Then MinHash on detected genes or a larger C is needed, and cost grows linearly.
- Allen labels are circular with PCA-based clustering. The Tahoe slice mitigates this, but cell lines separate too easily.
- Landmark bounds are loose in high intrinsic dimension, so the certified fraction may be small. Report it anyway.
- MICA installs are painful (Python 3.9, pinned 2021 dependencies) for the baseline runs.
- PI verdict: the most reliably finishable idea for a CS lead alone, with medium novelty. It is strongest merged with Idea 2 into one paper, where Idea 2 supplies the scientific finding and this idea supplies the scale.

ideas.title: What does cell-to-cell mutual information measure? Co-detection decomposition and depth-robust MI distances for MICA
ideas.one_line: Split MICA's cell-cell MI exactly into a co-detection term and expression-magnitude terms. Test whether MICA clusters are driven by dropout patterns and sequencing depth, and propose bias-corrected, depth-invariant MI distances. Evaluate them along a feature-count axis from 32 to 20,000 variables that maps onto the three course regimes.
ideas.problem_and_gap:
(1) MICA's estimator is a plug-in 2D histogram with equal-width bins between each cell's min and max, b = floor(G^(1/3)), and no bias correction or zero handling. I verified this in lib/distance.py on main on 2026-09-16: bins are set by each array's min and max, and distance = (H_joint - sum)/H_joint.
(2) With 80 to 95% zeros, the (0,0) cell of the joint table dominates. For 10x UMI data bin 0 holds only zeros, so the pattern of detected genes is a deterministic part of each binned cell.
(3) Binarized dropout patterns alone identify cell types about as well as HVG expression (Qiu, Nat Commun 11:1169, 2020, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-14976-9, verified via Europe PMC). MICA's reported edge may therefore come mainly from co-detection. Nobody has tested this.
(4) Nonzero bins depend on depth. One UMI maps to log2(1e6/N + 1), and each cell's max also moves with depth, so MI neighbors may be sorted by depth (hypothesis, UNVERIFIED). The Yu lab's own paper shows CPM normalization creates artifacts (Lu et al., Nat Commun 2025, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-56623-1).
(5) Prior work does not cover this:
- scMINER varied only the bin count (5 to 100).
- Skinnider 2019 found MI weak.
- The dropout-aware MI estimators that exist are gene-gene only: mixed KSG, Normi 2023, MIMIQ 2026.
- My 2026-09-16 Europe PMC check (MI + single-cell + clustering, 2025-2026) found no cell-cell estimator study.
(6) At low feature counts the estimator degenerates: 32 markers give b = 3 bins over 32 samples. The minimum usable p for MICA is unknown.
ideas.method_sketch:
1. Exact decomposition. It holds for plug-in estimates, because the chain rule holds for empirical distributions. With Dx = 1[bin > 0]:
   I(X;Y) = I(Dx;Dy) + I(X;Dy|Dx) + I(X;Y|Dy).
- Report the co-detection share I(Dx;Dy)/I(X;Y) for all pairs in the MDS-size datasets and for kNN edges at scale.

2. Depth-confound audit.
- Binomially thin the same cells to 25/50/75% of their UMIs, then measure kNN overlap and how many cells change cluster.
- Within ground-truth types, compute the partial Mantel correlation of D with |delta log depth|.

3. Estimator family. Every variant plugs into MICA-MDS and MICA-GE with nothing else changed.
- (a) Depth-matched: thin every cell to a common depth before binning.
- (b) Rank or quantile bins over nonzeros plus a dedicated zero bin. This is invariant to monotone per-cell rescaling.
- (c) Bias correction: Miller-Madow, and James-Stein shrinkage of the joint table (Hausser & Strimmer, JMLR 10:1469-1484, 2009, https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v10/hausser09a.html).
- (d) Normalization: NVI (1 - I/H joint) vs NID (1 - I/max H). Both are metrics (Vinh 2010), so the pruning in Idea 1 stays valid.
- (e) Ablations: MI over co-detected genes only (double zeros dropped), and binary-only I(Dx;Dy) or Jaccard.

4. Choose the recommended estimator with a label-free criterion (kNN stability under thinning), not by ARI, to avoid tuning on labels.
ideas.experiments:
The feature-count axis doubles as the course's three regimes.

D1, ordinary multivariate
- Levine_32dim CyTOF: 265,627 cells x 32 markers, 14 gated populations, about 104K labeled.
- Samusik_01: 86,864 x 39.
- Both from HDCytoData (https://bioconductor.org/packages/HDCytoData), arcsinh with cofactor 5.
- Optional middle point: the Hao 2021 CITE-seq ADT panel, about 162K cells x 228 proteins (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2021.04.048).
- Question: how low can p go, and does shrinkage rescue MI?
- Baselines: FlowSOM, PhenoGraph, Euclidean Leiden.

D2, >=2M cells
- Cao 2020 human fetal atlas: 4,062,980 cells x 45,676 genes, one 20 GB h5ad, CC BY 4.0 (https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aba7721). Very shallow sci-RNA-seq3, the extreme zero-dominated case.
- Per estimator: cluster a 200K-cell sketch with MICA-GE and propagate labels by kNN.
- Report co-detection share, depth confound, and ARI against the 68 CELLxGENE labels.
- Alternative: Allen MERFISH, 4.3M cells x 550 genes (a denser regime).

D3, high-dimensional
- CellBench 10x: 3,803 x 11,778, genotype truth (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-019-0425-8).
- Zeisel, Klein, Kolodziejczyk, and Chu 2016 (1,018 x 19,097).
- The scMINER datasets above 500 cells, so results line up with published ARIs.

Baselines: MICA default; Pearson and Spearman; proportionality rho_p (best in Skinnider 2019); Qiu 2020 binary co-occurrence clustering; PCA+Leiden; SC3s.

Metrics
- ARI and AMI at oracle K (comparable to scMINER) and at automatically chosen K;
- depth-confound score: variance of log UMI explained by cluster within true type;
- kNN stability under thinning;
- rare-type F1;
- co-detection share.

Thinning is applied only to UMI datasets.
ideas.compute_estimate:
Light, with no GPU required. Idea 1's kernel would speed everything up.
- MDS-size datasets (<=5K cells): 12.5M pairs x ~20K genes x ~8 estimator variants. A numba-parallel reimplementation on 120 cores should take minutes to under 1 h per dataset.
- Thinning replicates (3 depths x 5 seeds) multiply that by 15, still within one night.
- CyTOF: each pair is trivial. MICA-GE on 265K cells is about 2 to 4 h CPU per variant, extrapolated from HMC76K's 0.7 h on 40 cores.
- D2: a 200K sketch per variant takes about 2 to 4 h CPU; 4 to 6 variants fit in a few nights. Propagation takes minutes.
- Total: about 1 to 2 weeks of overnight jobs.

All runtimes are UNVERIFIED extrapolations.
ideas.novelty_claim:
Four claims.
1. An exact chain-rule decomposition showing how much of MICA's cell-cell MI comes from co-detection versus expression magnitude, measured from 32 to about 20K features.
2. The first test of sequencing-depth confounding in MI-based cell clustering.
3. Depth-invariant, bias-corrected MI distances that remain true metrics and plug into MICA.
4. An empirical minimum-feature-count guideline for MI cell clustering.

What a reviewer would check: the only dropout-aware MI estimator studies are gene-gene (Normi 2023, MIMIQ 2026), and scMINER tested only bin count.
ideas.closest_prior_work:
- Qiu, Nat Commun 2020: binary dropout patterns suffice (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-14976-9).
- Bouland, Mahfouz & Reinders, differential dropout analysis (bioRxiv 2021, https://doi.org/10.1101/2021.02.01.429187).
- Skinnider, Squair & Foster, Nat Methods 2019: MI weak among 17 measures.
- Watson et al., Brief Bioinform 2022 (https://doi.org/10.1093/bib/bbac387).
- Hausser & Strimmer, JMLR 2009: shrinkage entropy.
- Gao et al., NeurIPS 2017: mixed KSG (https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.06212).
- Normi (Brief Bioinform 2023, https://doi.org/10.1093/bib/bbad326).
- MIMIQ (bioRxiv 2026, https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.04.10.717770).
- Lu et al., Nat Commun 2025: transcriptome size.
- Vinh et al., JMLR 2010: NVI and NID are metrics.
ideas.risks:
- Effects may be small. MICA could already be depth-robust (scMINER showed robustness to bin count), which makes the audit a null result: still a useful short paper, but weaker.
- If co-detection dominates, the headline becomes roughly 'MICA is about Jaccard on detected genes', a critique of the chosen paper. For the course, frame it as an extension (better estimators).
- Low-p CyTOF MI will probably lose to Euclidean. Present it as a boundary, not a win.
- Oracle-K comparisons inherit scMINER's weak evaluation, so report automatic K too.
- Poisson thinning is invalid for Smart-seq read counts (Kolodziejczyk, Usoskin), so thin UMI datasets only.
- Moderate novelty. Estimator swaps can look incremental unless the decomposition result is striking.
- PI verdict: the highest chance of a clean finished story by December, and it pairs naturally with Idea 1.

- Journals: Bioinformatics, NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics, Briefings in Bioinformatics, BMC Bioinformatics.

- Fallback: an Entropy (MDPI) special issue on information theory in biology.

ideas.title: Honest scMINER: data thinning for oracle-free resolution selection and selection-aware hidden-driver inference
ideas.one_line: Replace MICA's oracle cluster count with a count-splitting merge test on MI clusters. Then check whether scMINER's hidden drivers survive when clusters, regulatory networks and differential activity are each computed on independent thinned folds of the same cells.
ideas.problem_and_gap:
(1) Published accuracy used an oracle. k was set to the true class count (MDS mode), or resolution was swept until the cluster count matched the truth (GE mode). On Zeisel, ARI ranged from 0.12 to 0.81 across resolutions. The docs chose PBMC14K's resolution from prior knowledge of the dataset (deep read).
(2) Hidden drivers are called by testing differential activity between clusters defined from the same cells, with per-cluster networks also inferred from those cells. That is the double-dipping pattern described by Neufeld et al. (Biostatistics 25:270, 2024) and Gao, Bien & Witten (JASA 2024, https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.2022.2116331). scMINER does not discuss it.
(3) 'Not differentially expressed' is declared from a non-significant test, which is not evidence that expression is flat.
(4) SJARACNe's developers argue in draft PR #73 (Aug 2026) that the consensus p-value is miscalibrated (from the deep-read report; not re-checked).
(5) Calibrated resolution methods exist but all assume PCA or Euclidean pipelines. None covers MI clustering or network activity:
- CHOIR (Nat Genet 2025, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-025-02148-8);
- sc-SHC (Nat Methods 2023, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-023-01933-9);
- recall (AJHG 2025, DOI confirmed via Europe PMC as https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ajhg.2025.02.014).
(6) My Europe PMC queries on 2026-09-16:
- count splitting or data thinning combined with regulatory network, regulon or TF activity: nothing relevant;
- count splitting or thinning plus clustering, 2024-2026: only an RNA-velocity stability paper (Li et al., Bioinform Adv 2026, https://doi.org/10.1093/bioadv/vbag104) and general methods.
ideas.method_sketch:
1. Split the UMI counts into independent folds with Poisson or negative-binomial thinning.
- References: NB count splitting (Neufeld et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.12985); generalized data thinning (Dharamshi et al., JASA 2025, https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.2024.2353948).
- Use two folds for clustering-only analyses and three folds (cluster / network / test) for driver analyses.

2. Over-cluster fold 1 with MICA (MDS with a large k, or GE at high resolution). Build a merge tree by average linkage on mean between-cluster MI distance.

3. Test merges bottom-up on a held-out fold.
- For each sibling pair, compute a two-sample statistic on held-out counts: balanced classifier accuracy as in CHOIR, or an energy statistic under the MI distance.
- Use a label-permutation null. It is valid because the folds are independent given the true means.
- Control family-wise error down the tree as sc-SHC does.
- The output is K with no oracle.

4. Selection-aware drivers.
- Build SJARACNe networks on fold 2 for each final cluster (downsample to 1,000 cells, or use SuperCell metacells as scMINER does).
- Compute activity and differential activity on fold 3.
- Hidden driver = significant differential activity on fold 3 AND expression shown equivalent by a TOST equivalence test within a pre-set margin (Schuirmann 1987), not merely non-significant DE.

5. Report calibrated p-values, plus a hidden-driver false-discovery rate estimated from null datasets.
ideas.experiments:
Null calibration (the headline figure)
Use homogeneous populations, where any cluster split or hidden driver is false:
- (a) single FACS-sorted populations from Zheng 2017 (https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms14049), such as CD14 monocytes or CD19 B cells;
- (b) a single cell line in DMSO control wells from Tahoe-100M (check the control labels);
- (c) scDesign3 simulations (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-023-01772-1).
Compare p-value QQ plots and false-positive rates for vanilla scMINER (forced K) against the thinned version.

D1: PBMC14K
- 13,605 x 17,986, 7 FACS populations. CD4 naive, memory and Treg partly overlap, which makes it a good test of under- and over-splitting.
- Optional: Hao 2021 ADT counts, where NB thinning applies.

D2: 2M-cell slice of Tahoe-100M
- CC0, 50 cell lines, demuxlet labels more than 98% accurate (https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.02.20.639398). K is known and the labels are not circular.
- Cluster a 200K sketch of fold 1, propagate labels, and run merge tests on fold 2 for all cells.
- Secondary: Allen WMB (2.3M), to see which taxonomy level (34 / 338 / 1,201) the chosen K lands on.
- No SJARACNe at 2M cells.

D3
- Zeisel (UMI; 7/9 and 47 labels), Klein (inDrop UMI), CellBench 10x (genotype truth).
- Do not thin read-count Smart-seq datasets.

Driver ground truth, reused from scMINER
- Perturb-seq knockouts (GSE221321), CRISPRa/i (GSE218988), CITE-seq (GSE164378).
- Precision and recall of drivers, vanilla vs thinned. Expect some loss of power.

Baselines for K: oracle MICA; MICA silhouette (-sil); CHOIR; sc-SHC testClusters applied to MICA labels; recall; scICE (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-60702-8); chooseR.

Metrics: type I error at alpha; |chosen K - true K|; ARI and AMI at the chosen K; wNMI; rare-type F1; driver precision against perturbation truth.
ideas.compute_estimate:
- Thinning costs one pass over the nonzero counts: seconds to minutes, even at 2M cells.
- MICA on folds: minutes for small datasets, about 6 min for PBMC14K, about 2 to 4 h CPU for a 200K sketch (estimate).
- Merge tests: permutation classifiers on subsampled pairs, a few CPU-hours in parallel on 120 cores.
- SJARACNe is the bottleneck: one network per cluster per fold.
  - With TF-only hubs, at most 1,000 cells or metacells, and 100 bootstraps, expect hours per network.
  - A user reported 160 to 200 GB for 1,361 cells (SJARACNe issue #50), so run at most 2 to 3 jobs at once.
  - Budget about 40 to 60 networks over 2 to 3 weeks of nights.
- No GPU needed.
- CHOIR on 2M cells may exceed 12 h, so run it on the sketch (runtime UNVERIFIED).
ideas.novelty_claim:
Two claims.
1. The first selection-aware (count-splitting) pipeline for inferring hidden drivers from network activity after clustering, with a measured false-discovery rate for the vanilla approach on homogeneous data.
2. The first significance-based, oracle-free resolution selection for MI-distance clustering, validated at 2M cells with non-circular labels.

What a reviewer would search for: count splitting or data thinning combined with VIPER, SCENIC, ARACNe, NetBID or scMINER. Nothing was found on 2026-09-16.
ideas.closest_prior_work:
- Count splitting (Neufeld et al., Biostatistics 2024) and NB count splitting (arXiv 2307.12985).
- Data thinning (Neufeld et al., JMLR 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.07276) and generalized data thinning (JASA 2025).
- CHOIR (Nat Genet 2025), sc-SHC (Nat Methods 2023), recall (AJHG 2025).
- ClusterDE (bioRxiv 2023, https://doi.org/10.1101/2023.07.21.550107).
- Selective inference for k-means (Chen & Witten, JMLR 2023, https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v24/22-0371.html).
- scICE (Nat Commun 2025).
- NetBID2 (Dong et al., Nat Commun 2023, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-38335-6).
- Li et al., count-splitting stability for RNA velocity (Bioinform Adv 2026).
